result.summary: Introduces an AssertUnreachable() macro in util/check.h that directly calls internal_abort_helper with noreturn semantics. Replaces falsy assertions (like assert(false) and Assert(false)) and naked aborts across the codebase using a scripted diff, cleans up dead code following unreachable blocks, and adds an assert_falsy linter rule.
result.problem: Unreachable branches guarded by assert(false) or Assert(false) cause toolchain issues: assert(false) triggers warnings under clang-cl and raises confusion regarding NDEBUG behavior, while Assert(false) obscures the noreturn attribute behind a function call and causes -Wreturn-type warnings under GCC. In addition, future use of C++23 std::unreachable() invokes undefined behavior instead of safely aborting.
evidence: PR description links a Compiler Explorer reproducer (https://godbolt.org/z/h7PT3jh3Y) showing -Wreturn-type and unreachable code diagnostics under GCC and clang-cl for the existing patterns.
result.scope_notes: Contains a scripted-diff commit touching dozens of files across the codebase and adds a Rust-based linter check in test/lint/test_runner.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a commit removing unused includes from src/test/util_tests.cpp based on review feedback and include-what-you-use output.
result.card: This PR introduces AssertUnreachable() to mark unreachable code and replaces falsy assertion patterns (assert(false) and Assert(false)) across the codebase, enforced via a new linter. It eliminates compiler -Wreturn-type and unreachable code warnings across GCC and clang-cl while avoiding the undefined behavior of C++23 std::unreachable(). Importance is supported by Compiler Explorer reproducers demonstrating compiler warnings with the existing assertion macros. It has no dependencies.

risk.why: A typo or misplaced assertion in the mechanical substitution could turn a recoverable condition into an immediate process abort.
